summary: Repair the malformed German clause about closing the city gates
before: und aus Angst die Stadttore schlössen
after: und schlossen aus Angst die Stadttore
rationale: This is a coordinated narrative main clause after die Einwohner der Stadt fürchteten sich vor ihm. It needs the finite verb before the object and the indicative past schlossen, rather than subjunctive schlössen. The correction preserves the participants, reason and action.

summary: Reviewed all 37 occurrences. Preserve existing sense1 combining bodily support and day-ending meanings; do not renumber or split the inherited sense.

The two inherited Preterit boxes encode different formations: gnele with an agent suffix versus unsuffixed gani with day subject. Existing gani examples are moved to Preterit Intransitive; repeated proposals of a new form are not accepted as a novel attestation.

Sunset gani appears as narrative temporal boundary and as completed boundary in a future instruction (PrS34/21). Dependent gone in JL16.7/19 is already quoted. PrS37/21 and PrS24/10 are also already represented despite page/text-reference differences; no duplicate examples added.

gnoyo remains in inherited Infinitiv. gnayte/gnete are feminine construct sunset nouns in temporal and directional phrases; Nomen Actionis records their attested nominal function while the precise paradigm relationship remains open.
103/11–13,44 repeatedly have ganyo ʕal i maṣa: the Turoyo supports a leaning state, but the ending can reflect a copular contraction rather than prove Part act. No new Part act. box is published.
No independent idiomatic phrase or light-verb collocation is established; sunset remains inside the inherited meaning, and ʕal gives the bodily support.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.

Jan supplies a clear I Infectum-wa gunewo in a duration question (Jan 2.2/194). There is no token-initial k-/gəd- prefix in gunewo; its initial g belongs to the root, contrary to the reader generic morphological wording.
gani remains Preterit Intransitive following round 1. Negated gani with heš (Jan 2.4/890,892) gives a sunset boundary not yet reached; it does not require a new tense box.

Jan 2.4/774 juxtaposes temporal gnayte d yawmo and finite Gani u yawmo. This directly supports keeping Nomen Actionis separate from Preterit Intransitive, while the relation of gnayte to gnoyo remains open.
